source.title: Beyond Coordinate Gauge: An Audited Protocol for Detecting Donor-Specific Functional Fingerprints after Neural Collapse

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-network representational alignment and residual variation in independently initialized networks using Procrustes alignment, reconstruction error, and donor-fingerprint identification, rather than the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on alignment fit, shared support, and whether donor-specific function remains identifiable after baseline correction. The within-seed Phase-1-to-TNC rank comparison does not directly compare representations across independently trained models, so it is not recorded as a cross-model convergence result. Exact donor-logit preservation on the donor’s own activations verifies the alignment construction, not cross-model similarity. Cited findings from prior studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Five MNIST MLP-5 networks differing only in seed are compared with orthogonal Procrustes plus affine head correction. The study measures held-out logit reconstruction error, shared supported-subspace dimension and donor-specific residual identifiability. This is a different method from either original, aimed at whether seed-different networks converge (V3), map linearly (V4) and converge incompletely (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that seed-different networks under Neural Collapse share a low-dimensional geometry, yet donor-specific functional fingerprints remain detectable after alignment and recipient-baseline correction. They say this is detectability only, not transplantability or causal persistence, and that generality beyond MLP-5/MNIST is untested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses affine-correct orthogonal Procrustes alignment, held-out logit reconstruction, and donor-fingerprint identification in a Neural Collapse setting; it is not a replication of either original source’s method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that the residual reconstruction error is stable under calibration resampling (ncal=1000), and that corrected identification margins remain close to the earlier leakage-affected margins. The query-dependent baseline was corrected to a template-only baseline; primary reported results use the corrected implementation.
record.problems: Five seeds, one architecture, and one dataset; training is a paper-matched reconstruction rather than an exact replication. Donor identification uses one fingerprint definition, with no comparison to alternative definitions beyond the per-class-accuracy control. No transplantation or continued-training intervention tests portability or causal persistence.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded the Phase-1-end versus TNC rank battery (Table 4 and Fig. 3), because it compares checkpoints within the same training trajectories rather than representations across independently trained models. Excluded cited findings from prior work.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no different architectures, objectives or data.
Only one architecture (MLP-5) on one task (MNIST), at Neural Collapse checkpoints. Unit- or feature-level matching was not tested.
Only orthogonal Procrustes was tested. Stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, cross-architecture maps and downstream-task loss were not tested.
No neuron, SAE-feature or circuit matching.
No comparison of similarity measures or out-of-distribution inputs. Calibration size was varied only for stability.
Plateau with scale and the causes of alignment (shared data or objective versus a common model of reality) were not tested.

missing.what: Shared supported-subspace dimension (r=45-50) and near-zero energy (eta about 0.000-0.002) outside the mapped projector, for seeds 0-2. This is the direct evidence of a shared subspace.
missing.locator: Table 5 (the text calls it Table 4); Results 3.3

missing.what: Additive donor-recipient model of the pairwise error matrix: R^2=0.755, leave-one-pair-out MAE 0.0150. Much of the pairwise misalignment is donor- or recipient-level.
Raw (uncorrected) fingerprint identification: 20/20 correct, minimum margin 0.0055.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this study, so verdicts apply. The ~13% residual error is attributed to the shared supported subspace, not null-space ambiguity (Table 3). The paper's table numbering in the text is inconsistent with the tables themselves. Table 5 logit errors (seeds 0-2) differ slightly from Table 6 means (e.g., 0.1397 vs 0.1398). The Phase-1 versus T_NC rank battery is correctly left out as within-seed. The study cites Li et al. 2016 as reaching a similar qualitative finding; that is cited, not a row.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model scale or capability, and no comparison across different architectures, objectives, datasets, or modalities.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language model comparison.

The study tests five independently initialized networks of one architecture on one task, using aligned support and functional fingerprints; it does not test recurring individual features or establish shared subspaces across a range of architectures or tasks.
Tests an orthogonal Procrustes fit with affine head correction. Does not test stitching, relative representations, mappings without paired calibration data, or other mapping methods.
No neurons, SAE features, or circuits are matched or tested for universality.
Does not systematically compare similarity measures, their settings, or in-distribution and out-of-distribution inputs.

Shows shared geometry and residual donor-specific variation in this setting, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause the alignment, whether it plateaus across scale, or how it generalizes to other settings.

rows.subject: MLP-5 seeds 0–4, aggregate across ordered donor-recipient pairs
rows.size_stated: five networks; each MLP-5 has five width-512 Linear-ReLU blocks and a 10-class head
rows.operation_detail: Matched disjoint probe fingerprints to donor templates after recipient-level baseline correction using the template split only.
rows.note: Aggregate result across all five recipient folds; all confusion matrices are diagonal. The study says this demonstrates detectable donor-specific function, not transplantability or causal persistence.
rows.check: Donor identification measures residual donor-specific variation after alignment. This is evidence of incomplete convergence (V7), not of shared features (V3) or map quality (V4). Removed V3 and V4.

rows.note: Positive margins indicate the correct donor template was nearer than the closest incorrect donor template.

relationships.condition: Five seed-different MLP-5 networks on MNIST at the Neural Collapse (T_NC) checkpoint
relationships.reason: The text (Table 5) shows a shared supported subspace of dimension 45-50 holding essentially all held-out energy. Orthogonal maps reconstruct logits with 12-19% error (R01-R20). Seeds share a subspace without being identical.
relationships.display_finding: A shared subspace of dimension 45–50 captured essentially all held-out energy, while orthogonal maps reconstructed logits with 12–19% error.

relationships.condition: Orthogonal Procrustes plus affine head correction, n_cal=1000, same-architecture seeds, MNIST
relationships.reason: Held-out relative logit reconstruction error is 0.124-0.195 across the 20 ordered pairs (R01-R20). The loss is stable under resampling and not due to null-space ambiguity, so the linear map is lossy rather than near-lossless.
relationships.display_finding: With 1000 calibration examples, held-out relative logit reconstruction error ranged from 0.124 to 0.195 across 20 ordered pairs and persisted under resampling beyond null-space ambiguity.

relationships.condition: Five seed-different MLP-5 networks on MNIST at T_NC; only the incompleteness part of V7
relationships.reason: After alignment and recipient-baseline correction, all 20 donors are identified (p=0.0083) with margins 0.86-1.30 (R21-R22). Convergence leaves donor-specific residual structure.
relationships.display_finding: After alignment and recipient-baseline correction, all 20 donor identifications succeeded, with p=0.0083 and margins of 0.86–1.30, revealing residual donor-specific structure.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Five seed-different MLP-5 networks on MNIST at T_NC; only the incompleteness part of V7
source_check.reason: The identification result attributed to R21–R22 establishes detectable residual differences, not that alignment remains far from complete. Table 8 reports 20/20 identifications, p=0.0083 and corrected margins 0.8618–1.2963; these are identification measures, not alignment magnitude. Plateauing and shared-data/objective causation are untested.
